text: Madame Loisel came to know the terrible life of the very poor, but she took her part bravely. <break time="0.8s" /> They sent away the maid and moved into a little room under the roof. <break time="0.8s" /> She washed the dishes, scrubbed the floors, and carried water up the stairs, stopping at every landing to breathe. <break time="0.8s" /> At the end of ten years they had paid everything back, with the interest and all. <break time="0.8s" /> Madame Loisel looked old now, with rough red hands, untidy hair, and a loud voice. <break time="0.8s" /> Sometimes, when her husband was at the office, she sat down by the window and thought of that evening long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> What would have happened if she had not lost that necklace, Who knows. <break time="0.8s" /> How strange life is, and how little is needed to ruin us or to save us. <break time="0.8s" /> One Sunday, walking on the Champs Élysées, she suddenly saw Madame Forestier, still young, still beautiful, still charming. <break time="0.8s" /> Now that everything was paid, she decided to tell her friend the whole story. <break time="0.8s" /> The friend did not recognize her at first and cried, Oh, my poor Mathilde, how you have changed. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, I have had hard days since I saw you, and all because of you, Mathilde answered. <break time="0.8s" /> When she explained everything, Madame Forestier stopped and took both her hands. <break time="0.8s" /> Oh, my poor Mathilde, But mine was false, It was worth at most five hundred francs.
